# ANES Time Series Cumulative Data File: agent index

Questions asked in three or more ANES Time Series studies, pooled into one file covering 1948 to 2024, with harmonized codes.

Publisher: American National Election Studies. Dataset id: `anes-cdf`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://electionstudies.org/data-center/. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the study year; `phase` is the pre- or post-election; `mode` is the mode.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `20260205`: 1948,1952,1956,1958,1960,1962,1964,1966,1968,1970,1972,1974,1976,1978,1980,1982,1984,1986,1988,1990,1992,1994,1996,1998,2000,2002,2004,2008,2012,2016,2020,2024. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.
